name: Finding Unknowns
tagline: Find the unknowns before they get expensive.
description: Thirteen portable workflows for surfacing blindspots, making decisions, testing assumptions, and reviewing what an agent built.
audience: Developers working with coding agents on unfamiliar code, ambiguous requirements, or changes that need stronger evidence.
features: Surface hidden context before choosing an approach.
Turn an uncertain technical assumption into a bounded experiment.
Investigate what green tests miss and preserve the evidence.
example: Before committing to this integration, test whether replaying the same webhook can create duplicate orders.
outcome: A reproducible experiment, a verdict limited to the tested conditions, and the decision that changes as a result.
limits: Discovery and packaging checks are distinct from behavioral evaluation. Eleven workflows draw on Thariq Shihipar’s essays; two are maintainer-designed extensions. Sources remain credited in the repository.

name: MCP Stateless Conformance
tagline: Inspect the protocol behavior behind the endpoint.
description: A reproducible conformance probe and public results for remote MCP servers against the 2026-07-28 specification.
audience: MCP server maintainers and integration developers who need observed behavior rather than a self-reported compatibility claim.
features: Review the public server corpus and recorded observations.
Distinguish conformant, legacy, gated, and unreachable endpoints.
Inspect the probe source and re-run it against an appropriate test corpus.
example: Does this server answer a cold request with the required stateless protocol surface?
outcome: A recorded response and a scoped conformance verdict, with inaccessible endpoints kept separate from demonstrated failures.
limits: Results are dated observations. Server counts and operator counts are different adoption signals. No license was declared in the repository files checked on September 9, 2026.

name: Awesome AI Workflows
tagline: Start with a workflow you can inspect.
description: A curated collection of AI workflow recipes with links, implementation context, and verification evidence from FlowStacks.
audience: Builders choosing an AI workflow and looking for a concrete starting point they can adapt to their own tools and constraints.
features: Explore recipes by the problem they address.
Follow links to the workflow and its supporting evidence.
Contribute useful recipes and corrections to the collection.
example: Find a workflow for this task, then inspect which parts were actually checked.
outcome: A reference recipe and its verification scope, ready to assess against your own workload.
limits: The collection’s selection and arrangement use CC0. Linked workflows and the FlowStacks platform retain their own terms. Recipe checks do not establish model quality for every workload.

name: Agent Stylebooks
tagline: Choose the writing system before the model chooses one.
description: Sixteen portable editorial systems that guide structure, clarity, and review around the reader’s actual task.
audience: Teams writing documentation, interface copy, public information, reports, or specifications with AI assistance.
features: Choose a stylebook by the artifact and the reader’s task.
Make information order and editing criteria explicit.
Keep source provenance and editorial limits visible.
example: Use google-developer-docs to turn these notes into a setup guide.
outcome: A guide organized around prerequisites and actions, with supplied facts and technical meaning preserved.
limits: These are independently written, community-maintained interpretations of public guidance, not official source-organization products. Third-party guides retain their own terms.

name: AI Watermarks Reality Check
tagline: Check the evidence. Keep the unknowns visible.
description: Seven agent skills for inspecting provenance, verifying supported credentials, and testing what survives a publishing pipeline.
audience: Teams handling AI-assisted media and documents who need to distinguish observed metadata, verified credentials, and unavailable evidence.
features: Inspect supported file and text provenance signals.
Separate credential integrity from signer trust.
Compare originals and derivatives without modifying the source.
example: Compare the original image and its published copy. Which provenance evidence survives, and what cannot be verified?
outcome: A scoped survival report that separates present, missing, verified, and unavailable evidence.
limits: This is not a universal AI-authorship detector. Unsupported or unavailable detectors remain unknown. Cryptographic verification requires suitable local tooling and trust configuration.

name: AI Cost-Cutter Skills
tagline: Make the cheaper path earn your trust.
description: Ten skills for investigating AI spend, routing work, trimming context, and comparing cheaper approaches with explicit checks.
audience: Developers reducing AI costs while preserving the behavior their workload actually needs.
features: Attribute spend before choosing a cost intervention.
Compare alternatives with criteria stated before the trial.
Keep deterministic checks separate from workload-specific quality claims.
example: Audit our token receipts, identify the expensive tasks, and propose one cheaper route with a check for quality loss.
outcome: An evidence-backed cost hypothesis and a workload-specific comparison, rather than an assumed saving.
limits: The repository runs deterministic proof blocks in CI. Actual model quality and cost must be measured on your workload; provider prices and limits can change.

name: Agent Arena Skill
tagline: Explore agent services through a documented interface.
description: A skill reference for discovering agent capabilities, inspecting profiles and reputation, and using Agent Arena’s hosted API.
audience: Developers integrating agent discovery and service comparison into agent workflows.
features: Search for agents by capability.
Inspect profile and reputation information.
Review the hosted API’s service and payment requirements.
example: Find agents with this capability and inspect their profiles before choosing a service.
outcome: Candidate profiles and documented API interactions for the caller to assess.
limits: This project describes a hosted API. Some operations incur charges or on-chain effects; follow the current API documentation. No license was declared in the repository files checked on September 9, 2026.

name: Accessibility Agent Skills
tagline: Find the regression. Fix the source. Prove the repair.
description: Seven portable skills plus CLI and MCP tools for accessibility evidence, conservative repairs, verification, and regression protection.
audience: Teams building interfaces with AI who want accessibility findings tied to reproducible states and source changes.
features: Capture scoped findings with Playwright and axe-core.
Verify a repair against the same page state and baseline.
Preserve focused regression tests for the repaired behavior.
example: Audit this checkout state, fix one confirmed issue in the source, and replay the same state to verify the repair.
outcome: Before-and-after evidence with resolved, remaining, and newly introduced findings kept distinct.
limits: Automated and agent-assisted checks cover a subset of accessibility barriers. They do not certify WCAG conformance or replace human accessibility testing.

name: Roll Credits
tagline: Give your coding session closing credits.
description: A native Claude Code Mod that turns session activity into scrolling movie credits, with edited files as the cast and tools in the thank-you list.
audience: Claude Code terminal users who want a lighthearted recap of a coding session.
features: Open a native credits pane with /credits.
Switch to a still view, replay the roll, or print credits as text.
Keep activity counters in memory without extra model calls or telemetry.
command:
claude plugin marketplace add smukh/roll-credits
claude plugin install roll-credits@roll-credits-marketplace
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 claude
outcome: A fictional sample roll to try immediately. Run /credits after working to see the session activity the Mod observed.
limits: Requires early-access function hooks; tested with Claude Code 2.1.272 in the terminal. File credits count successful Edit, Write, and NotebookEdit calls. Bash and external-editor changes are excluded. Statistics reset when the Mod reloads.

name: Skill Adapter
tagline: Keep the skills you like when you change models.
description: Adapt an existing agent skill for a target model while preserving its purpose, workflow, and supporting files.
audience: People reusing skills across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Kimi Code, and Hermes who want a reviewable copy tailored to an explicit target model.
features: One installable skill with profiles for GPT-6 Astra, Claude 5, and Kimi K3, plus a conservative generic fallback.
Creates a separate adapted package and an ADAPTATION.md change report; your source stays intact.
Preserves requirements, approval gates, tools, and resources. Asks for the target when reliable model identity is unavailable.
example: Use skill-adapter to adapt ./my-skill for GPT-6 Astra. Preserve its workflow and supporting files, and write a separate adapted copy with a change report.
outcome: An adapted skill package you can inspect alongside the original and install in your agent.
limits: Invoke the adapter explicitly. The GPT-6 Astra smoke evaluation checked workflow preservation; it does not establish performance gains across models. Source updates require re-adaptation; automatic upstream merging is not implemented.
